summary.headline: Sigachi Q1 FY27 revenue INR121.27 cr with EBITDA margin 13.6%; management reiterates FY27 guidance of INR650-675 cr revenue and ~18% EBITDA despite run-rate gap.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 total operating income was INR121.27 crore, with EBITDA of INR16.5 crore (13.6% margin) and PAT of INR8.14 crore (6.76% margin). MCC contributed INR82.74 crore, API INR21.68 crore and O&M INR13.06 crore. Average MCC realisation rose to INR241.36/kg from INR216/kg in Q4, while capacity utilisation was 76.8% across plants. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR650-675 crore revenue and ~18% full-year EBITDA margin, but the Q1 run-rate of ~INR121 crore implies a steep H2 ramp that the call did not fully reconcile.

segments.name: MCC (microcrystalline cellulose)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR82.74 crore, about 70% of Q1 sales per analyst math; realisation INR241.36/kg. Management attributed share loss to a ~6,000 TPA capacity reduction after a Hyderabad incident, and expects to regain share as capacity returns.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Revenue INR21.68 crore in Q1; management expects quarter-on-quarter improvement and cited Sparsentan, Bempedoic acid and other higher-margin molecules. Mgmt expects INR100-110 crore for the year, below the INR90-100 crore Q4 target framing for FY27 quarterly pace was not clarified.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: Revenue INR13.06 crore in Q1; described as a steady, scalable contributor with no further quantification.

segments.name: CCS (croscarmellose sodium)
segments.commentary: 1,800 TPA facility at Dahej SEZ under construction; management says it will be operational only in FY28. Indian CCS market estimated at ~$100 million, with realisation INR1,200-1,500/kg per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance unchanged at INR650-675 crore; management says H2 ramp will deliver it, but Q1 was ~INR121 crore versus ~INR160-170 crore per quarter needed.
Full-year EBITDA margin target ~18%, reiterated; management attributes margin expansion to fixed-cost leverage as revenue rises.
Dahej-2 12,000 TPA MCC expansion now targeted for Q2 FY28, delayed from earlier Q1 FY28/Q4 FY27 timelines; total cellulose-based excipient capacity to reach 30,000 TPA on commissioning.
FY27 capex more than INR100 crore; FY28 INR150-200 crore; funding via bank borrowing and a possible preferential equity issue (not finalised).

Insurance (business interruption) claim expected to be settled in full with some discount, or an ad hoc amount, by about September 2026; eligible amount INR16.5 crore against INR25 crore policy, with a further 3-4 months expected for receipt.
capex_capacity: Current cellulose-based excipient capacity 18,000 TPA, exports over 53.5% of production; debottlenecking (extra shifter/blender) to add about 1,600 TPA per management.
Dahej-2 MCC expansion of 12,000 TPA (INR106 crore cost per Q4 call) targeted Q2 FY28; total capacity to reach 30,000 TPA.
CCS facility 1,800 TPA at Dahej SEZ (INR93 crore), operational in FY28; primarily export-oriented, with export inquiries already received.
Management plans further unspecified capacity expansion of about INR50 crore beyond MCC and CCS projects.
Company is debt-free with no term loans currently; bankers ready to lend.
demand_pricing: Management says MCC demand is strong given regulatory approvals and quality; cited Asia Pacific MCC CAGR of 7-8% and market size ~$1.4 billion by 2035.
Realisation rose ~12% QoQ to INR241.36/kg; management attributed this to product mix shift toward higher-grade MCC used in formulations (cheaper grades declining).
Smokeless tobacco (snuff) MCC demand described as nascent; management declined to give a growth number.
CMC (key CCS raw material) to be bought from China rather than made in-house; management says in-house CMC would be costlier at the ~couple-thousand-ton scale.
Management said CCS margins would be well above MCC margins; analyst's 25%+ margin figure was confirmed as correct, though no official target was set.

qa_highlights.question: Is oversupply a risk with many Indian MCC players expanding capacity, and what is the pricing trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said regulatory approval and quality matter for export markets; realisation rose to INR241.36/kg from INR216/kg in Q4, attributed to quality-driven customer preference.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q1 revenue (~INR120 crore) well short of the INR650-675 crore run-rate, and is guidance changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no change in guidance; Q1 was on plan with only small variations, and revenue will rise in H2.

qa_highlights.question: How does ~76.8% utilisation reconcile with the 30,000 TPA expansion and FY27 targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plant needs shutdown/cleaning validation on product-mix changes; it expects run-rate above 95-96% by year-end on 18,000 TPA declared capacity (about 4,500 TPA per quarter).

qa_highlights.question: What is the bridge to INR650 crore revenue given MCC capacity limits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 19,600 TPA available capacity at INR241/kg plus API and O&M contributing more than INR200 crore; analysts found the math difficult to reconcile and management asked them to recalculate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and funding for the capex and insurance claim?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance settlement or ad hoc amount expected by about September; capex funded via borrowing or a preferential equity issue, not yet finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MCC margins rise structurally since 2019?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited industry consolidation (world number one changed hands twice; an Indian player bought by a European firm) and a shift in formulator demand toward higher-grade, innovative MCC grades.

financial_highlights.change: Mgmt quoted ~INR21 crore in Q&A; Q4 call target was INR90-100 crore for API

risks_watch: H2 ramp risk: Q1 revenue of ~INR121 crore versus ~INR160-170 crore per quarter needed for the INR650-675 crore guidance; management said guidance is unchanged but did not show a full bridge (its own math given on the call was disputed by analysts).

MCC capacity and utilisation: 76.8% utilisation on 18,000 TPA declared capacity; management expects run-rate above 95-96% by year-end, and the Hyderabad loss of ~6,000 TPA must be recovered before the Dahej-2 expansion adds capacity.
Dahej-2 12,000 TPA MCC expansion slipped from Q1 FY28/Q4 FY27 to Q2 FY28; management said no further delay is expected but a further slip is possible.

Insurance business-interruption claim: eligible INR16.5 crore against INR25 crore policy, with timing guided variously to September 2026 and a further 3-4 months for receipt; settlement may carry a discount.

Funding: FY27 capex above INR100 crore and FY28 INR150-200 crore; funding via bank borrowing or a preferential issue not finalised; warrant forfeiture history raises execution concern for a preferential issue.
Margin path: full-year EBITDA margin ~18% versus Q1 13.6%, implying a much higher H2 margin; management attributed this to fixed-cost leverage without quantifying it.
Receivable days at 93-94 versus target ~90 by year-end and 75-80 thereafter; working-capital trend to monitor.
CCS (1,800 TPA, Dahej SEZ) operational only in FY28; CMC sourced from China; 25%+ margin confirmed verbally but not formally targeted.

summary.management_tone: Confident on guidance and on the MCC demand outlook, with repeated assurances that the company is on track despite the weak Q1 run-rate. Evasive or non-committal on several specifics: the revenue bridge (management asked analysts to recalculate), the snuff/smokeless tobacco demand, the API timing and quarterly ramp, and the preferential issue, which was left unfinalised.

1,800 TPA CCS facility at Dahej SEZ

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance of INR650-675 crore is held, but Q1 was INR121 crore against roughly INR160-170 crore per quarter needed, and the call did not reconcile the H2 ramp; Dahej-2 12,000 TPA MCC expansion slipped to Q2 FY28 and CCS to FY28, with 76.8% utilisation and a 6,000 TPA Hyderabad capacity loss.
